title: "🔬 Mission 5: Your first research dataset"

::: {.mission-meta}
⏱️ About 10 minutes · do this in RStudio, using your Mission 1 project
:::

Time to put Missions 1–3 to work on something real.

## Get the data

Good news — you already have it. Remember `participants.csv`, the file you downloaded into `data/` back in [Mission 1](01-projects.qmd)? That's what you'll use here.

(Skipped that step, or can't find it? **[⬇ Download participants.csv](../downloads/participants.csv)** and save it into your project's `data/` folder now.)

## Import it

In `R/analysis.R`:

```r
participants <- read.csv("data/participants.csv")
```

Notice the shape of that path — `"data/participants.csv"` — it's the [Mission 2](02-paths.qmd) mental model again: start at 🏠, open `data`, find `participants.csv`.

::: {.callout-note}
## Notice what you *didn't* need
No `install.packages()`, no `library()` — reading a `.csv` is something base R can already do, no extra tools required. Later in the course you'll meet `library()`, which loads add-on **packages**: extra tools that give R abilities it doesn't have out of the box. Don't worry about what that means yet — we'll cover it properly on the course itself. For now, just notice that plenty of real work doesn't need it.
:::

## Get to know it

Don't analyze it yet — just look around, the way you'd skim a paper before reading it closely.

```r
participants             # print it
str(participants)         # what's the structure? how many variables, what types?
dim(participants)          # rows, columns
names(participants)        # just the column names
summary(participants)      # a quick five-number summary of each column
```

## Answer this from the output alone

Using what `dim()` or `str()` told you: **how many participants are in this dataset, and what does each row represent?** (Hint: look at the column names — `id`, `age`, `group`, `score`. One row is one *what*?)

You don't need to write the answer anywhere. If you can say it out loud in a sentence, you've done the mission.
